sentences.text: Annexure A1 is the Final Report.

2. The allegation in the final report is that the petitioner carried on the money lending business without obtaining license under the Kerala Money Lenders Act and lent money to various persons including CW1 and CW2 charging exorbitant interest and thereby committed the above offences.

3. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegation in the final report, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in its entirety, do not prima facie constitute the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 3 read with Section 17 of Kerala Money Lenders 2025:KER:39245 Act, 1958 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012 or make out any case against the petitioner.

entities.text: Kerala Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor submitted that there are materials on record to connect the petitioner with the crime and when a prima facie case is made out, the jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code cannot be invoked.
4. Annexure 1 is the final report.
The learned counsel for the petitioner made available to me copies of the statement of witnesses which form part of the final report.
CW1 Narayanan and CW2 Baburaj are the victims.
CW3 Sujatha Radhakrishnan is the mother of CW2.

CW1 stated in his statement that he borrowed a sum of 50,000/- from the petitioner on an exorbitant monthly interest of 3,500/-
and that at the time of the said borrowal, the petitioner collected signed blank cheques and election ID card from him.
He further stated that even though the entire amount with interest has been repaid, the petitioner did not give back the signed blank cheques and ID card demanding interest.
CW2 also gave statement in that line.
According to him, the sum borrowed was 1,45,000/-.
CW3 also supported the version of CW2.

The statements of CW1 to CW3 are sufficient to attract the 2025:KER:39245 ingredients of the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, Section 3 read with Section 17 of Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 and Sections 3 read with 4 of the Kerala C.P.Mohan Roy vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136957740/

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner was an employee of Kancor Ingredients Ltd., Angamaly and he was the Secretary of Kancor Employee's Union as well as the Kancor Employee's Union Welfare Society.
It is submitted that while he was officiating as the office bearer of the Society, all documents of the Society were kept in his office.

It is also his case that the Society used to give financial assistance to its members during the Onam season on security of signed cheques and the cheque belonging to Narayanan (CW1) is one among them.
The petitioner also relied on Annexure A2 letter given by the Secretary, Kancor Employee's Union Welfare Society.
It is submitted that the cheque seized by the police from the possession of the petitioner is one handed over to him by Narayanan.
The said defence is something to be proved during trial.
As the matter now stands, there are prima facie materials to attract the ingredients of the offences alleged 2025:KER:39245 against the petitioner.
It is settled that when a prima facie case is made out, the jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C cannot be invoked.
Accordingly, this Crl.M.C is dismissed.
Considering the fact that the petitioner is a senior citizen, if the petitioner files an application for personal exemption, the same shall be favourably considered by the trial court.
